q: An FC/FA must have acquired a permit to work and/or do business in the Philippines in accordance with the rules and regulations under which issuance?
o: The Commission's Guidelines for the Registration of Foreign Professionals (Res. No. 98-547)
The Code of Ethical Conduct (CEC)
The Government Procurement Reform Act (R.A. 9184)
The Intellectual Property Code (R.A. 8293)
n: The FC/FA must have acquired a permit to work and/or do business in the Philippines in accordance with the Commission Guidelines for the Registration of Foreign Professionals, Resolution No. 98-547. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.2.2)

q: Beyond being an RLA, an FPCA must also be:
o: A member in good standing of the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)
An officer of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE)
A member of the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture (PRBoA) itself
A registered contractor under the PCAB
n: The FPCA must be a member in good standing of the IAPOA, in addition to being a Philippine RLA and possessing FPC qualifications. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.1)

q: Besides an individual professional consulting architect (PCA), PACS may also be rendered through what kind of entity, as contemplated under Sec. 14.1.1?
o: A consulting firm, i.e., a Registered Architectural Firm (RAF)
A government procuring entity
A design-build contractor exclusively
A homeowners' association
n: Sec. 14.1.1 defines PACS as being rendered by a professional consulting architect (PCA) or by a consulting firm — i.e., a Registered Architectural Firm (RAF) — of independent advice, technical assistance, and related activities. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1)

q: SPP 209 requires that compensation and allowances for PACS be:
o: Set strictly below foreign consulting compensation standards
Comparable with foreign consulting service compensation standards
Fixed at the minimum wage rate under the Labor Code
Left entirely to the discretion of the Client with no reference standard
n: Sec. 14.3.3 provides that compensation and allowances shall be comparable with foreign consulting service compensation standards. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.3.3)

q: Which method of compensation under SPP 209 computes the PCA's fee as salary cost multiplied by a factor, plus direct cost or reimbursable expenses?
o: Retainer
Percentage of total project cost
Per Diem or Hourly Basis
Salary cost times a multiplier, plus direct cost or reimbursable expenses
n: Sec. 14.2.2.3 provides for compensation computed as salary cost times a multiplier, plus direct cost or reimbursable expenses. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.2.2.3)

q: No qualified FPCA is available for a highly specialized structural-architectural consulting engagement, so the Client engages a Foreign Architect (FA) instead. Under SPP 209, what additional requirement must be met in this situation?
o: A minimum of five (5) Filipino RLAs must be hired as co-signatories on all drawings
The FA must first obtain FPCA status within one (1) year of engagement
No additional requirement applies once a Foreign Architect is validly engaged
A minimum of two (2) Filipino RLAs in the same area or field of architectural specialization must be employed as understudies
n: Where no qualified FPCA is available and a non-FPCA (i.e., an FA or FC) is engaged instead, a minimum of two (2) Filipino RLAs in the same area or field of architectural specialization shall be employed as understudies. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.3)

q: Which is one of the qualification requirements for a Foreign Consultant/Foreign Architect (FC/FA) under Sec. 14.1.1.2?
o: The individual must be an FPCA in his or her home country
The individual must be a member of the IAPOA
The individual must satisfy the definition of a Professional Consulting Architect (PCA)
The individual must have Philippine citizenship by naturalization
n: Sec. 14.1.1.2.1 requires that the FC/FA satisfy the definition of a Professional Consulting Architect (PCA), as one of several cumulative requirements for that category. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.2.1)

q: For a Filipino architect to qualify as an FPCA, what registration status must he or she hold?
o: The individual must be a member of the Council of the Built and Natural Environment (CBNE) board
The individual must hold a foreign architectural license only
The individual only needs a valid PTR (professional tax receipt)
The individual must be a Philippine-registered and licensed architect (RLA)
n: The FPCA must be a Philippine-registered and licensed architect (RLA). Registration/licensure in the Philippines is a core qualification distinguishing the FPCA from unlicensed practitioners. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.1)

q: Professional Architectural Consulting Services (PACS) is governed by which SPP document, and under what section of the overall Standards of Professional Practice numbering does it fall?
o: SPP Document 208, discussed under Sec. 13
SPP Document 206, discussed under Sec. 11
SPP Document 207, discussed under Sec. 12
SPP Document 209, discussed under Sec. 14
n: Professional Architectural Consulting Services is SPP Document 209, treated under Sec. 14 of the Standards of Professional Practice — distinct from Comprehensive Architectural Services (SPP 206), Design-Build Services (SPP 207), and Architectural Design Competitions (SPP 208), which are treated in earlier sections. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14 (title))

q: How does SPP 209 treat compensation for PACS requiring only one kind of expertise/specialization compared to PACS requiring more than one type of expertise?
o: Multi-expertise PACS may not be compensated at all under SPP 209
Single-expertise PACS may only be compensated by retainer
They shall be treated differently, since the latter requires the use of more than one type of expertise
They must always be compensated at the same flat rate regardless of complexity
n: Sec. 14.3.2 states that compensation for PACS requiring only one kind of expertise/specialization or related types of expertise shall be treated differently from those services that require the use of more than one type of expertise. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.3.2)

q: A Client pays a PCA a fixed periodic amount to remain available for consulting services on an ongoing basis. This corresponds to which method of compensation?
o: Salary cost times a multiplier
Fixed/Lump Sum payment
Percentage of total project cost
Retainer
n: Retainer, under Sec. 14.2.2.2, is a method of compensation whereby the PCA receives a periodic fixed payment for ongoing availability of consulting services. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.2.2.2)

q: A developer is selecting a consulting architect for a specialized field of architectural practice regulated under the Council of the Built and Natural Environment (CBNE). Under SPP 209, who should generally render this PACS?
o: Any RLA regardless of specialization, since specialization is not considered under SPP 209
A duly-qualified Filipino Professional Consulting Architect (FPCA), since only FPCAs shall render PACS in such areas of specialization, except where no qualified FPCA is available
A general contractor, since CBNE areas fall outside architectural PACS entirely
A Foreign Consultant, since foreign expertise is always preferred for CBNE-regulated specializations
n: Only duly-qualified FPCAs shall render PACS in areas or fields of architectural specialization performed by members of the CBNE, except where no qualified FPCA is available — in which case a non-FPCA (FA or FC) may be engaged subject to the understudy requirement. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.3)

q: Under SPP 209, a Foreign Consultant (FC) or Foreign Architect (FA) is best described as:
o: A Philippine corporation with foreign shareholders
An architect who only practices outside the Philippines and has no PH engagement
An individual who is not a citizen of the Philippines but meets specified qualification and permit requirements
Any Filipino architect who has studied abroad
n: An FC or FA refers to an individual who is not a citizen of the Philippines, who must additionally satisfy the definition of a PCA and meet permit/registration requirements set out in Sec. 14.1.1.2. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.2)

q: Aside from being a Filipino citizen, what additional professional-consultant standing must an FPCA possess?
o: A permit to work issued under Board Resolution 98-547
Certification as a Foreign Architect (FA)
The qualifications of a Filipino Professional Consultant (FPC) as defined under the applicable rules
Accreditation as a Technical Advisor for design competitions
n: The FPCA must possess the qualifications of a Filipino Professional Consultant (FPC), in addition to being a Filipino citizen and a natural person, and the other requirements set under Sec. 14.1.1.1. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.1)

q: Which entities are required under SPP 209 to respect and take cognizance of the CEC and the SPPs on PACS compensation?
o: All entities in the Government, private sector, CSOs, and the international community with projects on Philippine soil
Only Filipino-owned private corporations
Only foreign consulting firms with a TSP
Only Government agencies
n: Sec. 14.3.6 provides that all entities, whether in the Government, private sector, or CSOs, and the international community (with projects on Philippine soil), shall respect and take cognizance of the CEC and the SPPs. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.3.6)

q: According to the Recommended Professional Fee provisions of SPP 209, the computation of compensation for PACS shall depend on:
o: The type of services to be rendered and the conditions under which they are to be performed
The number of years since the PCA's licensure
Only the size of the consulting firm's staff
Only the nationality of the PCA rendering the service
n: Sec. 14.3.1 provides that the computation of compensation for PACS shall depend on the type of services to be rendered and the conditions under which they are to be performed. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.3.1)

q: Which method of compensation under SPP 209 bases the PCA's pay on a daily or hourly rate?
o: Fixed/Lump Sum payment
Percentage of total project cost
Retainer
Per Diem or Hourly Basis
n: Sec. 14.2.2.1 lists Per Diem or Hourly Basis as one method of compensation, under which the PCA is paid according to a daily or hourly rate. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.2.2.1)

q: An FC/FA is also required to be:
o: A registered and/or licensed professional architect in his own country of origin (and/or country of residence/practice, as applicable)
Exempt from any home-country licensure requirement, provided he holds a TSP
A member of the Philippine Institute of Certified Public Accountants
A registered and licensed architect in the Philippines (RLA)
n: The FC/FA must be a registered and/or licensed professional architect in his own country of origin (and/or country of residence/practice, as applicable) — unlike the FPCA, who is licensed in the Philippines. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.2.3)

q: An FPCA engaged as a consultant signs and seals the architectural drawings submitted for a building permit application. If defects later arise from those documents, what is the FPCA's status and exposure?
o: Liability passes automatically to the Client since the Client owns the project
As the Architect-of-Record (AoR), the FPCA assumes the attendant professional responsibilities and civil liabilities for the project
Liability passes automatically to the Foreign Consultant supervising the project
The FPCA has no liability at all because PACS is merely advisory in nature
n: Signing and sealing architectural documents makes the FPCA the Architect-of-Record for the project, which carries the attendant professional responsibilities and civil liabilities under existing law — it is not liability-free simply because the engagement began as a consulting service. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.1)

q: Which of the following is a threshold requirement for a person to qualify as a Filipino Professional Consulting Architect (FPCA)?
o: The person must be a Filipino citizen and a natural person
The person must be employed by a foreign consulting firm
The person must hold a TSP (temporary/special permit)
The person must be a corporation registered with the SEC
n: An FPCA refers to a Filipino citizen, a natural person, who possesses the qualifications of a Filipino Professional Consultant (FPC) as defined, among other requirements. A TSP and being a non-citizen are instead features of the Foreign Consultant/Foreign Architect category. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.1)

q: PCAs are required to adhere to and be governed by relevant provisions pertaining to compensation as provided under which set of standards, per SPP 209?
o: The Codes of Ethical Conduct (CEC) and the other Standards of Professional Practice (SPP)
Only R.A. 9184 (GPRA)
Only the Labor Code of the Philippines
Only the National Building Code (P.D. 1096)
n: Sec. 14.3.5 provides that PCAs shall adhere to and be governed by the relevant provisions pertaining to compensation as provided for under the Codes of Ethical Conduct (CEC) and the other Standards of Professional Practice (SPP). (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.3.5)

q: A Client and a PCA structure an engagement so that part of the fee is a retainer for ongoing availability, and part is computed on a per diem basis for site visits. Is this arrangement consistent with SPP 209?
o: Yes, but only for Foreign Consultants, never for FPCAs
No — retainer and per diem arrangements are mutually exclusive under SPP 209
Yes — compensation may be computed based on one or a combination of the enumerated methods, with modifications applicable to the type of service and specific case
No — SPP 209 requires that only a single method of compensation be used per engagement
n: Sec. 14.2.2 expressly allows compensation to be computed based on one or a combination of the enumerated methods, with modifications applicable to the types of services and/or specific cases, if and when needed. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.2.2)

q: SPP 209 provides that compensation of a PCA may be computed based on one or a combination of methods. Which of the following is NOT one of the enumerated methods of compensation under Sec. 14.2.2?
o: Percentage of total project cost
Fixed/Lump Sum payment
A flat licensing fee paid annually to the PRC
Salary cost times a multiplier, plus direct cost or reimbursable expenses
n: Sec. 14.2.2 enumerates five methods of compensation: Per Diem or Hourly Basis, Retainer, Salary cost times a multiplier plus direct/reimbursable expenses, Fixed/Lump Sum payment, and Percentage of total project cost. An annual PRC licensing fee is not a method of computing professional compensation under this provision. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.2.2)

q: Which government agencies (among others) must allow the FC/FA to practice architecture in the Philippines under pertinent laws, rules, and regulations?
o: The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) only
The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) only
The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) and the Bureau of Immigration and Deportation (BID), among other concerned regulatory agencies
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) only
n: The FC/FA must be allowed by the DOLE, the Bureau of Immigration and Deportation (BID), and other concerned regulatory agencies and/or instrumentalities of government to practice the State-regulated profession of architecture in the Philippines. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.2.3)

q: An FPCA who signs and seals architectural documents for a project thereby becomes:
o: The Architect-of-Record (AoR) for that project, assuming the attendant professional responsibilities and civil liabilities
Automatically a Foreign Consultant for that project
Exempt from civil liability because the FPCA is only a consultant
The Professional Advisor for a design competition
n: If the FPCA signs and seals architectural documents, he or she becomes the Architect-of-Record (AoR) for the project and thereby assumes the attendant professional responsibilities and civil liabilities consistent with valid and subsisting laws. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.1)

q: Under SPP 209, PACS may be rendered by which of the following?
o: Only a Filipino Professional Consulting Architect (FPCA)
Only a licensed civil engineer acting as project consultant
Only a Foreign Consultant (FC) or Foreign Architect (FA)
Either a Filipino Professional Consulting Architect (FPCA), or a Foreign Consultant (FC)/Foreign Architect (FA)
n: SPP 209 recognizes two categories of persons who may render PACS: (1) a Filipino Professional Consulting Architect (FPCA), and (2) a Foreign Consultant (FC) or Foreign Architect (FA), each subject to its own qualification requirements. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.1 and 14.1.1.2)

q: A foreign consulting firm proposes a significantly higher fee than an FPCA for an identical scope of consulting work on the same project. Is this consistent with SPP 209's compensation provisions?
o: Yes — foreign consultants are always entitled to a premium under SPP 209
Yes — but only if the foreign consultant holds a TSP
No — SPP 209 requires the Foreign Consultant's fee always match the Retainer method exactly
No — for the same scope of work, there shall be no disparity in compensation between FPCAs and their foreign consultant counterparts
n: Sec. 14.3.4 requires no disparity in compensation between FPCAs and foreign consultants for the same scope of work; a significantly higher fee quoted solely because the consultant is foreign would run against this provision. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.3.4)

q: Which method of compensation ties the PCA's fee to a share of the overall project cost?
o: Fixed/Lump Sum payment
Per Diem or Hourly Basis
Percentage of total project cost
Retainer
n: Sec. 14.2.2.5 lists Percentage of total project cost as a method of compensation, computing the PCA's fee as a percentage of the overall project cost, comparable to the percentage-of-construction-cost method used in other SPP documents. Note: unlike SPP 206/207, Sec. 14 of SPP 209 does not itself specify a numeric percentage rate for PACS. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.2.2.5)

q: Under SPP 209, a PCA may provide services directly or indirectly to the Client in the manner:
o: Set exclusively by the Client without reference to any professional body
Fixed by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
Prescribed, suggested, or promulgated by the Commission/Board through the IAPOA
Solely dictated by the foreign consultant's home-country standards
n: A PCA may provide services directly or indirectly to the Client in the manner prescribed, suggested, or promulgated by the Commission/Board through the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.2.1)

q: Besides the general work permit, an FC/FA engaging in the practice of any branch of architecture for a project on Philippine soil must also secure:
o: Accreditation as a Technical Advisor under the ADC rules
A retainer contract approved by the IAPOA
A temporary/special permit (TSP), in full accordance with Board Resolutions implementing Secs. 37 and 38 of R.A. No. 9266
A certificate of good standing from the CBNE
n: The FC/FA must have acquired a temporary/special permit (TSP) to engage in the practice of any branch of architecture for any project on Philippine soil, in full accordance with the pertinent Board Resolutions implementing Secs. 37 and 38 of R.A. No. 9266. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.2.2)

q: An FPCA must also be an RLA specializing in any or several branch/es of the architecture profession as defined under which law?
o: R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) and its derivative regulations
R.A. No. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code)
R.A. No. 9285 (Alternative Dispute Resolution Act)
R.A. No. 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act)
n: The FPCA must be an RLA specializing in any or several branch/es of the State-regulated profession of architecture as defined under R.A. No. 9266 and its derivative regulations. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.1)

q: What does Professional Architectural Consulting Services (PACS) mean under SPP Document 209?
o: A design competition process for selecting an architect for a government project
The preparation of schematic design documents only, without any advisory function

The rendering by a professional consulting architect (PCA) or a consulting firm (e.g., a Registered Architectural Firm) of independent advice, technical assistance, and related activities requiring appropriate knowledge, skills, training, experience, competence, integrity, and/or financial and logistical capability
The act of directly supervising construction work on behalf of the Owner on a full-time basis
n: PACS is defined as the rendering, by a PCA or a consulting firm such as a Registered Architectural Firm (RAF), of independent advice, extension of technical assistance and services, and the undertaking of activities requiring appropriate knowledge, skills, training, experience, recognized competence, integrity, and/or financial and logistical capability. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1)

q: For the same scope of work, what does SPP 209 say about compensation between Filipino Professional Consulting Architects (FPCAs) and their foreign consultant (FC) counterparts?
o: FPCAs shall always be paid a lower rate to remain cost-competitive
There shall be no disparity in the compensation between them
SPP 209 is silent on this comparison
FCs shall always be paid a premium rate over FPCAs
n: Sec. 14.3.4 provides that for the same scope of work, there shall be no disparity in the compensation between FPCAs and their foreign consultant (FC) counterparts. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.3.4)

q: A Client and PCA agree on a single, predetermined total amount covering the entire scope of consulting services, regardless of hours spent. This is which method of compensation under SPP 209?
o: Retainer
Fixed/Lump Sum payment
Per Diem or Hourly Basis
Salary cost times a multiplier, plus direct cost or reimbursable expenses
n: Fixed/Lump Sum payment, under Sec. 14.2.2.4, is a single predetermined amount covering the full scope of the consulting engagement. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.2.2.4)

q: For Government projects, the selection of Professional Consulting Architects (PCAs) shall be in accordance with the relevant provisions of which law?
o: R.A. No. 9266, the Architecture Act of 2004
R.A. No. 8293, the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines
R.A. No. 9184, the Government Procurement Reform Act (GPRA) of 2003
R.A. No. 9285, the Alternative Dispute Resolution Act of 2004
n: For Government projects, the selection of PCAs shall be in accordance with the relevant provisions of R.A. No. 9184, otherwise known as the Government Procurement Reform Act (GPRA) of 2003. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 14.1.1.4)
